KNOWLEDGE STATE (before this tutor turn):
Target form: EN-F-A1-GR-word-order-svo (word order (subject + verb + object)). Learner level A2. First language Arabic.
Session 1.
W1 (wrong) strength 0: the verb can come first, as in Arabic. Its error: puts the verb before the subject ("Plays Ahmed football.").
W2 (wrong) strength 0: the adjective comes after the noun. Its error: puts the adjective after the noun ("I have a car red.").
C1 (correct) strength 1: a statement starts with the subject, then the verb, then the object. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: an adjective comes before its noun. Independent correct productions so far: 0.

PREVIOUS TUTOR TURN (the task set before the learner's message):
Rule: an English statement is subject + verb + object: "Ahmed plays football". An adjective goes before its noun: "a red car".

Look at this pair. Right: I have a red car. Wrong: I have a car red.

Now write one sentence of your own. Write one sentence about your friend and a big thing he or she has.

LEARNER'S LAST MESSAGE:
My friend has a big house.
FACT: the last learner message produced the form CORRECTLY.

TUTOR TURN TO JUDGE:
Yes, that is correct. Well done.

Write one sentence about your sister and a colour she likes on her clothes.
